# Planearby

> A free Vue 3 nearby-aircraft dashboard with Korean, English and Japanese interfaces.

Planearby starts when the page becomes visible and the user grants browser location permission. It polls aircraft positions every five seconds until stopped or the page is closed, with no thirty-second session limit. Background browser power policies can delay polling. Returning to the page triggers a refresh.

When GPS permission is unavailable, users can choose a map location or enter latitude and longitude. The picker is accessible below the radar, from settings, and from location error messages. Confirming a point scans real aircraft around that point without GPS permission. The manually selected center is labeled separately, kept in memory only, and is not overwritten by delayed GPS callbacks or stopped by GPS permission denial. Users can switch back to their device location from settings. Leaflet loads lazily when the picker opens; OpenStreetMap tiles use the browser cache and visible attribution. Tile requests reveal the viewed map area. Failed map loading does not prevent coordinate input.

On mobile, HTTP LAN addresses such as http://192.168.x.x are not secure contexts for GPS or orientation APIs. The compass permission request must follow a direct button tap. Level-phone orientation is required; relative-only orientation is not treated as north. Previously permitted active compass subscriptions resume when the page becomes visible again.

The radar plots aircraft relative to a manually selected facing direction or an explicitly enabled phone compass. Aircraft noses indicate received ground track. The default horizontal search radius is 25 km, configured in utils/geo.js; altitude is excluded. Supported Airbus, Boeing and Bombardier models are shown. GLEX, helicopters, ground aircraft, stale positions and unsupported types are excluded. Empty results do not prove there are no nearby aircraft.

An analog split-flap board shows one aircraft and rotates to an unseen aircraft every ten seconds. Track uses three cells and distance four cells. Missing route airports retain NON flap cells. Scheduled-time fields are omitted. Phone and tablet layouts place the radar above the board. Light and dark themes include the board and flap cells. Reduced-motion preferences disable the animation.

Data sources: adsb.lol positions under ODbL 1.0, accessed through the free keyless proxy.cors.dev relay in static builds because the source API lacks browser CORS; adsbdb reference routes; the Air Portal directory for operating Korean airlines; and generated OpenFlights airline and aircraft snapshots. Vite development uses the included fixed-upstream /api/aircraft function. VITE_AIRCRAFT_API_URL optionally selects a separately deployed function in production. The domestic directory takes precedence over missing or historically reused OpenFlights airline codes and supplies Korean names directly. Airline names and IATA/ICAO pairs are matched from generated datasets, not handwritten airline lists. Callsign-derived airline names and routes are inferred and may differ from the actual operation. No paid data API, API key, login or payment information is sent to data providers.

Approximate coordinates rounded to three decimal places are sent to cors.dev or the configured relay and adsb.lol. Exact browser coordinates are used locally for distance filtering. Requests omit credentials and referrers. App code does not store or log coordinates; relay and provider policies apply to requests. Theme, language and manual facing preferences are stored locally. Cached routes, deduplication and backoff reduce unnecessary calls. Short 429 limits honor Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Reset. A confirmed daily quota exhaustion opens a full-screen token-exhaustion dialog and stops scanning; restarting before the known reset shows the dialog without another request. Missing quota headers are treated as ordinary throttling, not proof of exhaustion. A 403 is retried after at least five minutes. Free access does not guarantee unlimited availability. Observed adsb.lol headers on 2026-10-28 included a 500-request daily policy; relay IPs may share that allowance. No automatic proxy switching bypasses limits.

GitHub Pages supports live tracking without an API URL, signup, keys or a separately deployed backend: the static JavaScript calls adsb.lol through cors.dev. Location permission is requested when the page becomes visible. After errors, the example-dashboard button displays twelve fictional aircraft only when clicked; examples never replace live observations silently. GitHub Pages cannot run server functions. The app is prerendered to static HTML and has semantic landmarks, keyboard controls, accessible status messages and generated deployment metadata. It is for personal curiosity, not navigation or safety decisions.

- [adsb.lol data](https://www.adsb.lol/docs/open-data/api/)
- [CORS relay documentation](https://cors.dev/docs)
- [adsbdb](https://github.com/mrjackwills/adsbdb)
- [OpenFlights](https://openflights.org/data.php)
- [Air Portal airline directory](https://www.airportal.go.kr/airline/airCompanyInfo.do)
